newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end down on loosening liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end down on loosening liquidity.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed lower on Wednesday as liquidity continued to return to the banking system following the Chinese new year holiday that ended on Monday, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate ended at 6.241 percent against Tuesday's 6.260 close, with 30-day commercial paper falling to 5.70-5.75 percent from 5.75-6.00.
Dealers expected the rates' post-holiday fall to continue, but the central bank may launch open market operations to mop up liquidity if the fall turns into a plunge.
The rates had been at annual highs due to strong demand for funds before the five-day Chinese new year holiday, but they fell sharply on Tuesday as cash demand eased.
Government bond yields were higher on profit-taking triggered by concerns over likely increases in the price of water and oil products in coming months, dealers said.
The 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 6.0550-6.0650 percent against 6.0480-6.0490.
